name: John Salvesen
bio: John Salvesen is the Republican nominee for Georgia's 5th Congressional District. Originally from South Jersey, he has lived in Atlanta since 1994 and has worked in the construction industry. He was the Republican nominee for the same seat in 2024, his first run for office.

platform.point: Supports using paper ballots to secure elections.
Pledged not to own stocks or accept corporate donations if elected.

notes: Appears on some listings as John "Bongo" Salvesen; platform points come from his 2024 campaign, and his former site bongoforcongress.com no longer hosts campaign content.

name: Lucy McBath
bio: Lucy McBath has represented Georgia in the U.S. House since 2019, serving the 6th District (2019-2023 and since 2025) and the 7th District (2023-2025). Born in Joliet, Illinois, she worked as a Delta Air Lines flight attendant before becoming a gun-safety advocate. She serves on the Judiciary and Education and the Workforce committees.

platform.point: Backs background checks on every gun sale and transfer, and red flag laws.
Wants to strengthen the Affordable Care Act, expand Medicaid and lower the Medicare eligibility age to 55.
Supports raising the federal minimum wage to $15 an hour.
Opposes vouchers for private schools.
Has sponsored legislation for stricter police accountability rules.

economy.evidence: Supports a $15 federal minimum wage and criticized the 2017 Republican tax cuts.

welfare.evidence: Supports Medicaid expansion and lowering Medicare eligibility to 55, while preferring to shore up the ACA over Medicare for All.

liberty.evidence: Supports abortion rights including public funding (abortion), while backing universal background checks and red flag laws (guns).

security.evidence: Sponsored stricter police accountability rules and favors rehabilitation services over punitive approaches.

immigration.evidence: Supports raising high-skill and family visa caps and opposes abolishing ICE; voted for the Laken Riley Act in 2025.

tech.evidence: Supports net neutrality rules for an open internet.

name: Kevin Martin
bio: Kevin Martin is the Republican nominee for Georgia's 6th Congressional District after defeating Justin Pinker in the May 2026 primary. He is an accounting and finance professional who works as a controller in Smyrna. He holds bachelor's degrees from the Georgia Institute of Technology and Georgia State University.
notes: No campaign website or published issue positions were found.

name: Rich McCormick
bio: Rich McCormick has served in the U.S. House since 2023, first for Georgia's 6th District and since 2025 for the 7th. Born in Las Vegas, he served about 20 years in the Marine Corps and Navy, flying helicopters and later as a Navy medical officer. He is an emergency physician with a medical degree from Morehouse School of Medicine.

platform.point: Aims to curb federal spending and debt, lower taxes and reduce regulation.
Calls for enforcing border security and existing immigration laws.
Prioritizes parental involvement, school transparency, academic standards and local control.
Seeks to expand access to medical professionals and reduce bureaucracy between patients and doctors.
Supports military readiness, servicemembers and key alliances.
Supports transparent election processes and clear voting rules.

economy.evidence: Campaign calls for lower taxes, fewer regulations and less federal spending.

welfare.evidence: Has called for large cuts across Social Security, Medicaid and Medicare spending and criticized blanket free school lunches.

liberty.evidence: Cosponsored a 2025 bill recognizing personhood from conception (abortion) and favors fewer gun limits (guns).

security.evidence: Supports keeping qualified immunity for police officers.

immigration.evidence: Campaigns on enforcing border security and immigration laws and has backed a border wall.

foreign.evidence: Campaign emphasizes military readiness and key alliances; sponsored a resolution defending Israel after October 7.

energy.evidence: Supports fracking and expanded domestic energy production.

education.evidence: Campaign stresses parental involvement, transparency and local control of schools.

notes: Security and energy scores rest on earlier OnTheIssues research that was not re-verified in this pass; the faith score was removed for lack of specific evidence.

name: Tony Kozycki
bio: Tony Kozycki is the Democratic nominee for Georgia's 7th Congressional District and is from LaGrange, Georgia. He is a former U.S. Navy aviator who flew three combat deployments and served as a liaison to the Royal Australian Air Force. He is an attorney who graduated from Georgia State University College of Law in 2021.

platform.point: Pledges to push a ban on congressional stock trading on his first day in office.
Proposes a plan to lower childcare costs, expand housing access and make one full-time job enough to support a family.
Wants to lower costs, protect coverage and hold insurers accountable for premium increases.
Pledges to protect Social Security and Medicare and fight prescription costs and scams aimed at seniors.
Supports securing the border while reforming the immigration system.
Pledges better access to veterans' care and benefits.

welfare.evidence: Pledges to protect Social Security and Medicare and lower health care costs while protecting coverage.

immigration.evidence: Calls for border security alongside reform of the immigration system.

foreign.evidence: Emphasizes strong alliances and international partnerships for national security.

name: Austin Scott
bio: Austin Scott has represented Georgia's 8th District in the U.S. House since 2011 and serves on the Agriculture, Armed Services, Rules and Intelligence committees. Born in Augusta, he served in the Georgia House of Representatives from 1996 to 2011. He has worked in business as president of Southern Group LLC.

platform.point: Opposes tax increases and supports a balanced budget amendment.
Has consistently supported military aid to Ukraine.
Backs domestic oil production including offshore drilling and opposes climate taxes.
Sponsored a bill setting wage floors for H-1B visas and ending the Optional Practical Training program.
Supports repealing and replacing the Affordable Care Act.

economy.evidence: Voted for the 2017 Tax Cuts and Jobs Act and signed the Taxpayer Protection Pledge.

welfare.evidence: Supports ACA repeal, work requirements for welfare and photo ID for food stamps.

liberty.evidence: Opposes abortion (supports a 20-week ban), opposes same-sex marriage (LGBTQ), though opposes background check requirements (guns).

security.evidence: Received a mid-range rating from police accountability groups; sits on the Intelligence Committee.

immigration.evidence: Opposes a pathway to citizenship and birthright citizenship and sponsored a bill ending the OPT program.

foreign.evidence: Consistently voted for military aid to Ukraine, while favoring conditions on UN funding.

energy.evidence: Signed the No Climate Tax Pledge and supports offshore drilling.

education.evidence: Supports school vouchers including DC Opportunity Scholarships.

notes: The security score rests on limited evidence (a police-accountability group rating).

name: Kelly Esti
current_role: Navy veteran, education leader and small-business owner
bio: Dr. Kelly Esti is the Democratic nominee for Georgia's 8th Congressional District. He is a Navy veteran with a PhD who has worked as an education leader, small-business owner and chief financial officer.

platform.point: Focuses on affordable access to learning, from K-12 support to workforce training for working adults.
Treats health care as essential infrastructure and backs federal support for rural clinics and specialty care access.
Prioritizes road maintenance, transit options and broadband expansion.
Backs VA oversight, health care access and support for military families tied to Robins Air Force Base.
Supports federal labor standards and workplace protections.
Wants to modernize utilities and explore renewable options to lower long-term household costs.

economy.evidence: Supports federal labor standards and workplace protections.

welfare.evidence: Treats health care as essential public infrastructure and backs federal support for rural clinics.

energy.evidence: Supports modernizing utilities and exploring renewable energy options.

education.evidence: Emphasizes K-12 support, workforce development and affordable learning programs for adults.

notes: The campaign also links a Facebook page and a TikTok account, but their exact URLs could not be confirmed.

name: Andrew Clyde
bio: Andrew Clyde has represented Georgia's 9th District in the U.S. House since 2021. He served 28 years as a U.S. Navy officer, including three combat deployments, and retired as a commander in 2013. He founded the Clyde Armory gun store in 1991.

platform.point: Supports replacing the income tax with the FairTax and dismantling the IRS.
Opposes any compromise on Second Amendment rights.
Holds that life begins at conception and backs legislation protecting the unborn.
Wants to eliminate the Department of Education and the EPA and return their functions to states.
Champions limits on government seizure of property after the IRS seized funds from his business.
Prioritizes delivering promised care and benefits to service members.

economy.evidence: Supports the FairTax (H.R. 25), abolishing the IRS and shrinking government.

welfare.evidence: Voted against the PACT Act expanding VA benefits for toxic exposure.

liberty.evidence: Opposes abortion from conception (abortion) while strongly opposing gun restrictions (guns).

immigration.evidence: Called in 2026 for barring Muslim immigration and for denaturalizing and deporting Muslim citizens.

energy.evidence: Campaign calls for eliminating the Environmental Protection Agency.

education.evidence: Campaign calls for eliminating the federal Department of Education.

faith.evidence: Opposed honoring Judge Joseph Hatchett, citing Hatchett's ruling that blocked prayer at public schools.

notes: Energy was newly scored from his call to eliminate the EPA.

name: Caitlyn Gegen
bio: Caitlyn Gegen is the Democratic nominee for Georgia's 9th Congressional District. She holds bachelor's and master's degrees from the University of Georgia and a master's from the London School of Economics. She describes herself as a community organizer who has worked on women's rights and criminal justice reform.
notes: Her campaign site showed no issue content when checked; local coverage of her statements on ICE activity in Athens could not be accessed.

name: Houston Gaines
bio: Houston Gaines is a member of the Georgia House of Representatives, serving District 117 from 2019 to 2023 and District 120 since 2023. Born in Athens, he graduated from the University of Georgia in 2017, where he was student government president. He is the Republican nominee for Georgia's 10th Congressional District.

platform.point: Calls for deporting immigrants who commit crimes and full cooperation with ICE.
Supports law enforcement and opposes efforts to defund police.
Supports balanced budgets, tax cuts and eliminating wasteful federal spending.
Backs small businesses and domestic manufacturing to keep jobs in the U.S.
Wants to protect farmland from foreign acquisition and advocate for farmers.
Opposes congressional insider trading.

economy.evidence: Campaigns on tax cuts, balanced budgets and cutting federal spending.

liberty.evidence: Opposes abortion funding and transgender sports participation (abortion, LGBTQ) while backing constitutional carry (guns).

security.evidence: Campaigns on supporting police and cracking down on crime, and backed efforts to hold district attorneys accountable.

immigration.evidence: Calls for deporting criminal immigrants, ICE cooperation and border security.

foreign.evidence: Supports peace through strength, rebuilding the military and support for Israel.

tech.evidence: Co-sponsored Georgia's version of the GENIUS Act setting stablecoin rules to promote financial innovation.

faith.evidence: Earlier research recorded his vote for Georgia's Religious Freedom Restoration Act.

notes: The Commons headshot is credited to the Georgia House of Representatives without a specific free licence, so it was not used. The faith score rests on earlier research not re-confirmed in this pass.

name: Pamela DeLancy
current_role: Retired Army colonel and registered nurse
bio: Pamela DeLancy is the Democratic nominee for Georgia's 10th Congressional District. She is a retired U.S. Army colonel with 39 years of service and a registered nurse.

platform.point: Proposes a Real Deal Act covering affordable health care, a living wage, retirement security, childcare and long-term care.
Wants accessible, affordable health care and protection of veterans' benefits.
Focuses on housing and food affordability and protecting water resources as data centers expand.
Favors prevention and partnerships among community leaders, educators and law enforcement.
Supports border security, oversight of agent conduct and legal work pathways that keep families together.

economy.evidence: Real Deal Act proposes a living wage requirement and broad federal support for working families.

welfare.evidence: Real Deal Act seeks affordable health care, childcare and long-term care for all families.

immigration.evidence: Backs legal work pathways, family unity and oversight of enforcement alongside border security.

energy.evidence: Prioritizes protecting water resources as data centers expand.

name: John Cowan
bio: Dr. John Cowan is the Republican nominee for Georgia's 11th Congressional District. He is a neurosurgeon and small-business owner who describes himself as a conservative outsider.

platform.point: Wants to fix problems he attributes to Obamacare by lowering premiums and expanding patient choice.
Proposes tax relief for families and small businesses and strengthening domestic industries.
Supports proof of citizenship to vote and transparency in ballot counting.
Pledges to protect free speech, freedom of worship and Second Amendment rights.
Supports banning congressional stock trading, stronger ethics rules and term limits.

economy.evidence: Proposes tax relief for families and small businesses.

welfare.evidence: Opposes Obamacare and favors more patient choice in health coverage.

liberty.evidence: Pledges to protect Second Amendment rights (guns) and free speech (speech).

notes: He appears to be the same John Cowan who ran for Congress in GA-14 in 2020, but this was not confirmed. The liberty score reflects only guns and speech; his abortion stance was not found.
